**JOB SUMMARY**
===============

The Chief Information Officer (CIO) for Shasta Community Health Center will lead the centralized Information Technology (IT/Informatics) service through an Information Technology Shared Services Organization. The CIO will provide technology vision and leadership for developing and implementing information technology in all IT/Informatics initiatives. This individual is responsible for the planning and execution of an information technology vision, goals and IT/Informatics initiatives that support the long-term objectives, mission and vision of Shasta Community Health Center (SCHC). This leader will collaborate and manage a team of professionals who are accountable for the delivery of all information technology services in the organization. The CIO will be a member of the Senior Management Team and report to the Chief Executive Officer.

* Develops a service level organization that establishes service standards for each entity served by the EMR.

* Establishes and maintains a service orientated, customer-focused IT/Informatics function that supports ongoing operations that drive efficiency, quality, customer service and growth.

* Ensures that enterprise information systems operate according to internal standards, external accrediting agency standards and legal requirements.

* Ensure cybersecurity risks are proactively identified, assessed, and mitigated.
* Lead vulnerability management, incident response coordination, security governance, and remediation activities.
* Partner with internal and external stakeholders to maintain a strong security posture across the organization.

* Maintain and continuously improve the Information Security Management System (ISMS).
* Lead activities supporting ISO 27001 certification and compliance.
* Ensure policies, controls, documentation, and supplier practices align with regulatory and organizational requirements.
* Support audits and ensure timely resolution of findings and corrective actions.

* Build trusted relationships with executives, business leaders, and operational teams.

The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) is the largest Fire Department in the United States and universally is recognized as the world's busiest and most highly skilled emergency response agency. The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs. FDNY members are sworn to serve and protect life and property and the Department works to continually educate the public in fire, life safety and disaster preparedness, along with enforcing public safety codes. Since its inception in 1865, FDNY has helped lead efforts to make New York the safest big city in the nation. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values.
  
  
The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) seeks a full-time Deputy Chief Information Security Officer (Deputy CISO) to serve within the Bureau of Enterprise Technology (BET). Reporting to the CISO, the Deputy CISO will assist in leading FDNY's cybersecurity program and protecting the Department's systems, networks, infrastructure, applications, and data. The successful candidate will support the development and implementation of cybersecurity strategies, policies, standards, and controls; identify and mitigate information security risks; and help ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of critical technology resources. The Deputy CISO will coordinate the investigation, containment, remediation, and recovery of cybersecurity incidents and support disaster recovery, business continuity, and technology resiliency efforts. The position will provide security oversight for networks, systems, cloud environments, applications, and technology projects and ensure compliance with applicable City policies, cybersecurity requirements, and industry standards. The Deputy CISO will also manage and provide direction to cybersecurity staff, consultants, contractors, and vendors. The Deputy CISO will work closely with the CISO, CIO, technology teams, agency leadership, City partners, and external stakeholders to strengthen FDNY's cybersecurity posture, promote security awareness, and support the Department's critical public-safety mission.
